ANALYSIS: “Complex partial seizure” is an older ILAE (International League Against Epilepsy) terminology (pre-2017 classification) that has been replaced by the more precise and descriptive term “focal onset impaired awareness seizure”. The updated classification emphasizes onset location (focal), level of awareness (impaired), and etiology when known. Temporal lobe epilepsy is the most common cause of focal impaired awareness seizures, and “cryptogenic” appropriately indicates presumed structural/functional abnormality where no definitive lesion is identified on current imaging — a standard and acceptable descriptor in clinical epilepsy practice.

Thus, the predicted diagnosis is not only synonymous with the reference diagnosis but represents an *updated, more accurate, and clinically preferred* terminology aligned with current ILAE guidelines. It adds relevant localization (temporal lobe) and etiologic context (cryptogenic), without overinterpreting or contradicting available evidence.
